items.title: How AI Is Reshaping China's Industrial Policy
items.content: Can Chinese tech companies help the country achieve technological self-reliance while keeping up in the AI arms race? On this episode, we speak with Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. Thornton China Center and author of the High Capacity newsletter, about Beijing’s response to the global AI boom and the tensions between Chinese companies’ commercial ambitions and the government’s long-term plans. He explains how companies draw on shared expertise and supply chains to expand across industries including smartphones, robotics, EVs and semiconductors — and we also discuss Huawei’s efforts to compete with Nvidia and why technological success doesn’t necessarily translate into strong returns for stock investors in China.  (Source: Bloomberg)

He explains how companies draw on shared expertise and supply chains to expand across industries including smartphones, robotics, EVs and semiconductors — and we also discuss Huawei’s efforts to compete with Nvidia and why technological success doesn’t necessarily translate into strong returns for stock investors in China.  (Source: Bloomberg)

summaries.zh: 文章探讨了中国科技公司如何在实现技术自给自足的同时参与AI军备竞赛。作者Kyle Chan分析了北京对全球AI浪潮的应对策略，以及中国公司商业目标与政府长期规划之间的张力。他指出，企业通过共享专业知识和供应链拓展至智能手机、机器人、电动汽车和半导体等领域。文章还讨论了华为与英伟达的竞争，以及中国技术成功并未必然带来股市高回报的现象。
summaries.en: China's industrial policy leverages tech companies to achieve technological self-reliance amid the AI arms race, balancing commercial goals with government plans. Companies like Huawei collaborate through shared expertise and supply chains in sectors such as smartphones, robotics, EVs, and semiconductors. However, success in technology doesn't always correlate with strong stock market returns. The discussion highlights tensions between corporate ambitions and national strategy. (98 words)

items.title: Anthropic Researcher Claims to Solve Riemann Problem With Claude
items.content: On the heels of Anthropic PBC’s record-breaking initial public offering, a researcher at the company said he believes he used its artificial intelligence software to solve a famous number theory problem that has plagued mathematicians for more than 150 years.

The announcement comes shortly after Anthropic's record-breaking IPO. The claim involves leveraging AI to address the hypothesis, which has eluded mathematicians for over 150 years.

items.title: Wall Street Week | Gaming Blockbuster, Healthcare Costs, Cybersecurity Meets AI
items.content: This week, former New York Fed President Bill Dudley and Kathryn Judge of Columbia Law School discuss what the Treasury and Fed can do to tackle the nation’s debt crisis. Plus, what Grand Theft Auto 6’s release means for a video game industry that routinely faces layoffs, delays and slowing consumer spending. Later, surging healthcare costs affect businesses and their employees as Americans choose their insurance policies for the year ahead. And, how is AI changing the cybersecurity stakes for small businesses? (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Hindlian Advisory CEO on AI & Anthropic Market Sell-off
items.content: Amanda Hindlian, Founder and CEO of Hindlian Advisory and Former Global Head of Capital Markets at the New York Stock Exchange, says Anthropic’s IPO should be judged separately from a volatile week for markets. She notes that investors had been uncertain about the pricing and overall execution just two weeks earlier, but the offering priced well, drew a significantly oversubscribed book—estimated at five to seven times—and traded strongly on its first day. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: US Credit-Fear Hits 8-Month High as Tech Angst Roils Markets
items.content: Measures of perceived US credit risk reached levels not seen in nearly eight months and the cost of protecting the debt of some of the biggest tech firms against default jumped on Friday, as the wobbling AI trade spurred volatility in global markets and sent investors piling into safe havens.

summaries.en: US credit risk measures hit an eight-month high as investors grew wary of tech firms, particularly AI, amid market volatility. items.title: Wall Street Reels as AI Fears Erupt; Nasdaq 100 Near Bear Market
items.content: Wall Street reeled on Friday as nagging concerns about the AI trade, which propelled US stocks from one high to the next for much of the year, turned into a full-blown, market-wide selloff. Anthropic PBC slumped after soaring in its public-market debut, while Nvidia Corp. sank 14%, pushing the Nasdaq 100 to the brink of a bear market.

items.title: JPMorgan Gets Lowballed Below 80 Cents for Qualtrics Hung Debt
items.content: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is fielding rock-bottom offers from investors as it weighs a potential debt sale tied to an acquisition by Qualtrics International Inc.

summaries.en: JPMorgan is considering a debt sale related to Qualtrics International's acquisition, receiving low offers below 80 cents on the dollar. Investors are submitting rock-bottom bids as the bank evaluates the potential transaction.

items.title: Nvidia Employees Complained About Huang's Behavior Years Ago
items.content: Ian King, Bloomberg News US semiconductor reporter, said that a lawsuit from two former Nvidia employees shows the price employees paid for the remarkable success achieved by former CEO Jensen Huang, as his behavior is scrutinized after allegations of multiple affairs. Huang's representatives said that the allegations in the complaint are from a long time ago and aren't a representation of Huang's behavior and how he's thought of inside Nvidia.  (Source: Bloomberg)

summaries.zh: 据彭博社报道，两名前英伟达员工提起的诉讼显示，前CEO黄仁勋为英伟达的辉煌成就付出的代价。随着多项婚外情指控的曝光，黄仁勋的行为受到审视。英伟达代表称，诉讼中的指控是多年前的旧事，不代表黄仁勋的行为及他在英伟达的为人。
summaries.en: A lawsuit from two former Nvidia employees alleges past inappropriate behavior by CEO Jensen Huang, now under scrutiny amid affair claims. Ian King of Bloomberg notes the suit highlights the personal costs employees faced for the company's success. Huang's representatives dismiss the allegations as outdated, stating they don't reflect his current standing at Nvidia. (49 words)
